messages.text: Sunday, November 8 · Canton, Michigan
Oboe recitals and henna patterns under a quiet November sky

Saturday brings overcast skies and a gentle chill to Canton as we settle into the rhythm of the season. Local attention turns toward cultural gatherings in Ann Arbor and the ongoing conversation around regional environmental policy.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 57 degrees and a low around 32 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:16 AM and sets at 5:19 PM, with a new moon that is 1.3 percent illuminated.
A day for artistry and connection
Connect with the community at the Henna Night at Betsy Barbour House at 2:00 PM, or attend Sara LeBlanc's master's degree oboe recital at the Earl V. Moore Building at 7:00 PM.
Mark your calendar for the 862 Meeting scheduled for November 11 at 6:30 PM.
Policy shifts and regional transitions

Congresswoman Debbie Dingell is moving to introduce a Data Center Bill of Rights to address infrastructure and environmental concerns in the district. Meanwhile, the region reflects on the historic election of Abdul El-Sayed to the U.S. Senate.
Looking toward the week ahead
Keep your schedule open for the 862 Meeting taking place this coming Tuesday evening.

Monday, November 9 · Canton, Michigan
Bingo mathematics and the quiet arrival of an overcast Sunday

The day brings a steady, gray stillness to Canton as we settle into a quiet autumn pace. Local curiosity turns toward the intersection of probability and play, while our science update examines the deep shifts in Earth's history.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 55 degrees and a low around 38 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:17 AM and sets at 5:18 PM, under a new moon that is 0.2 percent illuminated.
A day for curiosity and open stages

Consider the Math Grad Show and Tell Seminar on the asymptotics of bingo at East Hall in Ann Arbor at 3:00 PM. Later, The Ark hosts an Open Stage night at 8:00 PM for those looking to share music in a supportive setting.
A community meeting is scheduled for November 11 at 6:30 PM.
Investment in local resource hubs

The KeyBank Foundation has committed a 250,000 dollar investment to expand the Shelter Association of Washtenaw County's warming center and resource hub in Ypsilanti. This funding is intended to support daily operations and food costs for adults experiencing homelessness.
